title: Register a vehicle for local personal property tax
question: I moved to Albemarle or bought a vehicle. How do I get it on the county tax rolls?
office: Department of Finance & Budget, Office of Revenue Administration (Business & Personal Tax Unit), County of Albemarle. Under the county executive form there is no elected Commissioner of the Revenue or Treasurer: the Director of Finance assesses and collects the tax.
summary: Albemarle taxes vehicles normally garaged in the county, and its Department of Finance & Budget assesses and bills them. First title or register the vehicle with Virginia DMV, showing Albemarle as the garage jurisdiction, within 30 days of moving or buying. Then send the county's personal property registration form, on paper or online, to the Office of Revenue Administration. There is no decal. The county values vehicles at the J.D. Power clean trade-in value, taxes them at $4.28 per $100 (2026), prorates by month and applies car tax relief to qualifying vehicles. A yearly license fee goes on the June bill. Bills are due June 25 and December 5; vehicles added mid-year get a supplemental bill.

steps.step: Title and register the vehicle with Virginia DMV, with Albemarle County as the garage jurisdiction
steps.who: Vehicle owner; Virginia Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)
steps.how: If you moved here from another state, register and title the vehicle with DMV within 30 days of your move. State law lets a new resident drive a passenger car, pickup or panel truck, moped, autocycle or motorcycle that is registered for the current year in the other state, on that state's plates, for the first 30 days of residency (Va. Code § 46.2-662(A)); it does not cover other vehicles. A non-Virginia-resident active duty service member whose vehicle is registered and titled in another state need not title or register it in Virginia (Va. Code § 46.2-600). The county's Moving Personal Property page adds that after registering you will need a Virginia State Inspection. If you moved from another Virginia locality, update your mailing address and garage jurisdiction with DMV, and say when you moved into the county. If you bought the vehicle, apply to DMV for the title within 30 days of the purchase. Check that the DMV record says the vehicle is garaged in Albemarle County, because the county works from DMV's records. The county pages give DMV's number as 804-497-7100. The county no longer issues a decal.
steps.deadline: within 30 days of your move (county FAQ); within 30 days of the purchase or transfer (Va. Code § 46.2-600); change of address within 30 days (Va. Code § 46.2-606(A))
steps.fee: DMV title and registration fees, set by the state (not covered here)

steps.step: New resident: send the county a personal property registration form
steps.who: Vehicle owner, to the Department of Finance & Budget, Office of Revenue Administration (Business & Personal Tax Unit)
steps.how: After DMV, register the vehicle with the county so it goes on the tax rolls. The Moving Personal Property page says you have to tell the County you moved, whether you are moving in or out, and asks owners coming from another state and from another Virginia county alike to submit a registration form after updating DMV. Use the Personal Property Registration form (f1) or the county's online form (f2). The paper form asks for the vehicle's year, make, model, weight, type, personal or business use, purchase price and date, title number and VIN, the date it entered the county and your former residence. It also asks for each owner's name and Social Security number or federal ID (the form says disclosure is mandatory), the mailing address and the vehicle's location if different. Military owners give their home-of-record state, with a current Leave and Earnings Statement if they claim a domicile outside Albemarle. Leased vehicles need lessor and lessee details. Sign the declaration and mail the form to 401 McIntire Road, Suite 133, Charlottesville, VA 22902, or email it to Tax@Albemarle.org. If you only moved within the county, update DMV and give the county your new mailing address.
steps.deadline: none stated by the county for moving in; the form cites County Code § 15-801 (a new return when status changes), whose text was not read. The state May 1 return date (Va. Code § 58.1-3518) is for property owned on January 1; for a vehicle that gains a situs here after January 1, state law leaves the filing of returns to the local proration ordinance (Va. Code § 58.1-3516(B)), which was not read

steps.step: Bought a vehicle while living here: tell DMV, then the Office of Revenue Administration
steps.who: Vehicle owner (buyer); Virginia DMV; Office of Revenue Administration (Business & Personal Tax Unit)
steps.how: Report the purchase to DMV within 30 days. Then contact the Office of Revenue Administration (434-296-5852 or Tax@Albemarle.org) so it can update your account and billing. The registration form (f1) has fields for the purchase price and date. The county bases assessments on the date DMV received the information. If the new vehicle replaces one you sold or traded, report the sale to DMV yourself: refunds follow the sale date DMV records, and the county warns you not to rely on the buyer or the dealer to report it. A vehicle bought after the county prepares its bills is billed on a supplemental bill (step s8).
steps.deadline: within thirty days of purchase or transfer (DMV, per the county page and Va. Code § 46.2-600)
steps.fee: county vehicle license fee (step s7); state law gives purchasers at least a 10-day grace period from the purchase date to pay local license fees (Va. Code § 46.2-752(I))

steps.step: Check whether the vehicle is taxed elsewhere or exempt (students, out-of-state domicile, military, disabled veterans, special plates)
steps.who: Vehicle owner; the Department of Finance & Budget decides
steps.how: Full-time students: a vehicle garaged here while you attend college may be taxed in your home domicile; the county may ask for proof that the tax was paid there. Owners domiciled in another state are not taxed here if they show they paid personal property tax on the vehicle in that state. Service members whose home of record is not Virginia: all vehicles owned or leased by the member or spouse are exempt, with proof (LES or a statement from the commanding officer) every year. Veterans rated 100% service-connected, permanent and total: one passenger car, pickup or panel truck registered for personal use is exempt, including one owned by a married couple if either spouse is the veteran; leased and business-owned vehicles do not qualify. Apply on form f3 with the VA documentation (the form also accepts VA documentation that the veteran is paid at 100% as unemployable, and lets you tick a box if the county's Real Estate Division already holds it), returning it by mail, email or fax as the form directs; reapply only when the vehicle changes. Under state law the exemption ends on the veteran's death and does not pass to a surviving spouse. Permanent antique and vintage plates are exempt from both tax and license fee. Disabled Veterans tags, Prisoner of War tags and farm vehicles are exempt from the license fee only. National Guard members get 50% off the license fee. Ask the office about vehicles of certain nonprofits, and about the county's existing personal property tax program for members of volunteer fire departments and emergency medical services agencies (a 2026 staff report says the program exists but is not yet in the County Code).
steps.deadline: military proof every year; the veteran exemption applies from the date the vehicle is acquired or January 1, 2021, whichever is later

steps.step: The county values the vehicle and taxes it by the month
steps.who: Department of Finance & Budget, Office of Revenue Administration (the Director of Finance holds the commissioner of the revenue's powers)
steps.how: Cars, trucks and motorcycles are valued at the J.D. Power (formerly NADA) clean trade-in value as of January 1. Trailers, boats, motor homes and aircraft are valued at a percentage of the purchase price. Albemarle prorates. If you moved from a prorating locality, tax here starts on the date you moved in. If you moved from a non-prorating Virginia locality, you keep paying that locality through December 31 and the vehicle is taxable here from January 1 of the next year, but a vehicle you buy after the move is taxable here from the purchase date. Under state proration rules more than half a month counts as a full month. If a vehicle is not reported in time, state law says the assessing official 'shall' enter its fair market value from the best information he can obtain and assess it as if it had been reported (Va. Code § 58.1-3519).
steps.deadline: status and value fixed as of January 1 (the tax day), or as of the day the vehicle gets a situs in the county

steps.step: Car tax relief (PPTR) is applied automatically to qualifying vehicles
steps.who: Department of Finance & Budget; the vehicle owner checks the bill
steps.how: Relief covers up to the first $20,000 of value of a passenger car, motorcycle, or pickup or panel truck with a registered gross weight of up to 10,000 pounds. The vehicle must be owned by an individual (or leased by an individual under a contract that makes the individual pay the tax), used less than 50% for business, and carry a DMV 'passenger' plate type. The exemptions page treats a vehicle as used for business if more than 50% of its mileage is claimed as a business expense or more than 50% of its depreciation is deducted. Relief was 42% for tax year 2025; the county recalculates the percentage each year. Motor homes, mopeds, all-terrain vehicles, boats, trailers, farm-use vehicles and vehicles of 10,001 lbs or more on DMV's records do not qualify. The county gives no reduction for mileage. If the vehicle is qualified wrongly, contact the office (434-296-5852 or Tax@Albemarle.org). A vehicle found to be used for business can get a supplemental bill reversing the relief.
steps.fee: relief percentage set each year (2025: 42%, on up to the first $20,000 of value)

steps.step: The yearly vehicle license fee is added to the June 25 bill
steps.who: Department of Finance & Budget (bills); vehicle owner (pays)
steps.how: Each vehicle or trailer registered in the county pays a yearly license fee, which replaced the old decal. It appears on the first-half bill due June 25: $40.75 for cars and trucks of 4,000 lbs or less, $45.75 for 4,001 lbs or more, $28.75 for motorcycles, $18.00 for trailers of 1,500 lbs or less and $28.50 for heavier trailers. The rules are in County Code Chapter 15, Article 14 (§§ 15-1400 to 15-1409, including § 15-1402 on new vehicles and § 15-1405 on prorating), which was not read. State law caps the fee at the state fee in effect on January 1, 2020.
steps.fee: $40.75 (4,000 lbs or less), $45.75 (4,001 lbs or more), $28.75 (motorcycles), $18.00 (trailers 1,500 lbs or less), $28.50 (trailers 1,501 lbs or more)

steps.step: Pay the regular bills, or the supplemental bill for a vehicle added mid-year
steps.who: Department of Finance & Budget, Office of Revenue Administration (bills and collects); vehicle owner (pays)
steps.how: Regular bills are due June 25 and December 5; a due date on a weekend moves to the next business day. A vehicle bought or moved in after the county generates the bills goes on a supplemental bill, mailed 2 to 3 times a year with its own due date; the county says a supplemental bill may in some cases include amounts for three prior years as well as the current year. Pay online at albemarlecountytaxes.org, by phone at 866-820-5450, by mail to County of Albemarle, P.O. Box 7604, Merrifield VA 22116-7604 (postmarked by the due date), at the 24/7 kiosk or in person at 401 McIntire Road (Monday to Friday, 8 am to 5 pm), or in a drop box (no cash). E-checks are free; cards carry a convenience fee. The county's penalty policy says not getting a bill does not excuse late payment. Late payment costs 10% or $10, whichever is greater, plus 10% a year interest. Unpaid taxes can lead to a DMV registration hold, tax liens, debt set-off and a collection agency. State law requires the locality to allow an automatic extension of personal property tax on a qualifying vehicle owned by a member of the armed services deployed outside the United States, until 90 days after the deployment ends (Va. Code § 58.1-3916).
steps.deadline: June 25 and December 5; a supplemental bill has its own due date
steps.fee: $4.28 per $100 of assessed value (calendar year 2026), less car tax relief; license fee on the June bill; late payment penalty 10% or $10, interest 10% a year

steps.step: If the vehicle was damaged on January 1, file a vehicle assessment appeal
steps.who: Vehicle owner, to the Business & Personal Tax Unit
steps.how: Use the Notice of Appeal of Vehicle Personal Property Assessment (f4) only for a special condition on January 1, such as accident damage, heavy rust or a lost engine, that the J.D. Power value does not reflect. A detailed, itemized damage and repair estimate is always required: written on business letterhead by an insurance adjuster, auto appraiser or auto repair facility, with that person's name, address, phone number and signature, and describing each damaged condition that existed on January 1 and how much it reduces the J.D. Power clean trade-in value. To show the damage existed on January 1, either the estimate must say the condition existed in January of the tax year, or you may add photos of the damage taken in January of that year. Excess mileage alone is not enough. Mail the form and documents to 401 McIntire Rd, Suite 133, Charlottesville, VA 22902, or email Tax@albemarle.org. The appeal counts only when every document has arrived, and it must be filed again each year. The Department of Finance and Budget reviews it and notifies you of its decision; any refund is issued once the appeal process is complete. Pay the bill on time anyway. Wrong vehicle details are fixed by calling or emailing the unit, not by appeal.
steps.deadline: none stated; the condition must have existed on January 1 of the tax year, and adjustments do not renew automatically

steps.step: If the assessment is wrong for another reason, ask in writing for a correction
steps.who: Vehicle owner, to the Department of Finance & Budget (the assessing official)
steps.how: Write to the Department of Finance & Budget asking for a correction of the assessment, for example if the vehicle was not garaged in the county, was taxed for the wrong months, or should have had car tax relief or an exemption. The county's pages list no required contents for a correction request. Its appeal-rights sheet (f5) asks administrative appeals to give the taxpayer's name and address, federal tax identification number, local tax account number, a power of attorney or letter of representation if someone else files, a copy of the assessment, a detailed explanation and the relief requested, sent to Department of Finance & Budget, Attn: Revenue Administration - Assessments Unit, 401 McIntire Road, Room 133, Charlottesville, VA 22902; giving the same details with your evidence is a sensible way to make the request complete. You may ask for the facts and law behind the decision in writing. The county says you can go to the Circuit Court at any point. See the escalation routes for the deadlines.
steps.deadline: within three years from the last day of the tax year, or within one year from the date of the assessment, whichever is later (Va. Code § 58.1-3980(A))

caveats: Albemarle County's website (www.albemarle.org) refuses automated readers, so the county pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them before you act. The County's Terms and Conditions bar reposting its content without written permission, so the County's own words are not reprinted on this page; each step links the County page instead.

The county's online registration form (f2, forms.office.com) refuses automated readers, so its fields, and whether it is still in use, are not confirmed. The aircraft form on the Purchasing and Selling page is also on forms.office.com. That page also links a paper aircraft registration form (https://www.albemarle.org/home/showpublisheddocument/28596/639032168764730000), which has not been checked; aircraft are outside this vehicle process, apart from the valuation and rate notes.

Two editions of the paper form are linked. The Moving Personal Property page (May 2026 snapshot) links the Business & Personal Tax Unit edition (f1). The Personal Property Taxes & Fees page (August 2026 snapshot) links an older Assessments Unit edition (f6), which gives a different office mailbox and '434-296-5851 opt. 3'. The f1 edition shows tel 434-296-5851, while the county pages give 434-296-5852 for the Business & Personal Tax Unit and 434-296-5851 for payments. Both forms carry the same fields.

No county deadline for registering a vehicle after moving in or buying was found. The 30-day deadlines on the county pages are for DMV (title, registration and address change, which state law also sets in Va. Code §§ 46.2-600, 46.2-606 and 46.2-662). The county asks for a copy of a new state's registration within 30 days of moving away, but gives no deadline for moving in. The form cites County Code § 15-801 for a new return when status changes; Va. Code § 58.1-3518.1(B) lets a locality require one. The text of § 15-801 was not read, so any deadline or penalty it sets is unknown. The state return date is May 1 unless an ordinance sets another (Va. Code § 58.1-3518).

County Code not checked. The county's County Code page links its Code of Ordinances on Municode, whose CivicPlus terms forbid automated access and copying. Section numbers come from the county's form (§ 15-801), its Important Dates and Deadlines page (§§ 15-103, 15-104) and Legistar records (Article 8, personal property tax; Article 14, County Vehicle Licenses, §§ 15-1400 to 15-1409; § 15-101 due dates). The local quotes are from those county pages and a Legistar staff report, not from the Code text.

Tax rate and relief year: the Personal Property Taxes & Fees page (August 2026 snapshot) and the Tax Rates page give $4.28 per $100 for 2026. A proposal to raise the 2026 rate to $4.43 (Legistar 26-240) was held by the Board on April 15, 2026. The exemptions page (March 2026 snapshot) lists car tax relief rates only through 2025 (42%). Confirm the current year's relief percentage with the office.

Supplemental bill due date: the county page says only that supplemental bills have different due dates. A 2021 staff report (Legistar 21-461) proposed making supplemental property tax bills due within 45 days of the bill date. Whether that was adopted, and the current period, were not confirmed. State law lets a prorating locality bill partial-year taxes on or after December 15, with a due date at least 30 days later (Va. Code § 58.1-3516(B)).

Vehicle license fee: how the fee is prorated for a vehicle added mid-year (County Code § 15-1405, 'Prorating') and what § 15-1402 ('New vehicles required to obtain a license') requires were not read. The amounts are from the Personal Property Taxes & Fees page. Volunteer fire and EMS members: a staff report (Legistar 26-381, introduced August 24, 2026, agenda date September 16, 2026) asked the Board to schedule public hearings on ordinances setting a $0.00 personal property tax rate and a $0.00 license fee for one vehicle owned or leased by each qualifying active volunteer fire or EMS member. The Legistar history records that on September 16, 2026 the item 'was scheduled with the Consent Agenda'. The hearing date and outcome were not found. The same report says the county already runs such a program, not yet in the County Code, and that under state law the chief's certification is due by January 31 each year (Va. Code § 58.1-3506(A)(15), which also lets the assessing officer accept a late certification for good cause). The current program's terms were not found on a county page.

Military: the county's exemption for service members whose home of record is not Virginia rests on the federal Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, which is not in the 'va' index and is not quoted. The state deployment extension (Va. Code § 58.1-3916) is quoted.

Whether Albemarle has adopted the optional local penalty of up to $250 for a vehicle not registered in Virginia after a new resident's first 30 days (Va. Code § 46.2-662(B)) was not found. Whether the § 15-103(C) failure-to-file penalty is charged on late individual vehicle registrations was not found either.

Payment Options page inconsistency: the online and in-person sections list credit cards at 2.50% and debit cards at 2.35%. The phone section lists 'Debit Cards2.50%' and 'Credit Cards2.35%', which is the other way round. The kiosk section gives 2.5% for credit cards. The fee entry records the online and in-person rates.
Town of Scottsville: the county and the town signed a 2021 agreement on the county collecting the town's motor vehicle license taxes (Legistar 21-510). Town residents' fees are not covered here.

Who decides: under the county executive form the Director of Finance holds the powers of the commissioner of the revenue and the treasurer (Va. Code §§ 15.2-521, 15.2-522). The county's Important Dates and Deadlines page says the same, and the appeal-rights sheet refers to the 'Albemarle County Assessing Official'. Which official signs correction decisions was not stated.

Va. Code § 58.1-3912(C), a 30-day bill-mailing rule, covers county-executive counties contiguous to an urban county executive county. That is understood not to include Albemarle, so the 14-day rule in § 58.1-3912(A) is recorded. This was not checked against a county source.

Privacy: the Circuit Court Clerk's page names the Clerk and Chief Deputy Clerk, and some county forms give a finance mailbox. Staff names are not recorded. Only the office's published unit mailboxes (Tax@, payments@) and the unit's booking page are kept.

Local page quotes keep the county's own spacing and punctuation, including the unbalanced parenthesis in the § 15-103(C) sentence. DMV's own title and registration fees and documents are not covered here (state agency).

corrections: Method: the 50 state-law quotes (46 original, 4 added) were matched against I.text_of for each cited section, whitespace normalised only, and placed under the cited subsection by reading the section text. The 31 local quotes were matched against the official pages re-fetched read-only: www.albemarle.org again answered HTTP 403 (robots.txt included), so the same Internet Archive snapshots named in sources were fetched in raw (id_) mode, at about one request every few seconds with the lexflow-research User-Agent; the Legistar texts came from webapi.legistar.com (no robots.txt). The two PDF quotes (f1, f4) were read from the snapshot PDFs. All 81 matched word for word.

s5: the draft said the county 'can still assess' an unreported vehicle. Va. Code § 58.1-3519 says the commissioner (here the Director of Finance) 'shall' assess it from the best information he can obtain. The wording now follows the statute.

s6: 'owned by a person' is now 'owned by an individual', as the county FAQ says (Va. Code § 58.1-3523: 'natural person'). Added all-terrain vehicles to the non-qualifying list (county FAQ), the exemptions page's business-use test (more than 50% of mileage claimed as a business expense or more than 50% of depreciation deducted), and that the county recalculates the relief percentage each year.

s1: the draft said state law lets a new resident drive on the other state's plates for 30 days without limit. Va. Code § 46.2-662(A) covers only a passenger car, pickup or panel truck, moped, autocycle or motorcycle registered for the current year in the other state; the step now says so. Added the § 46.2-600 exception for non-Virginia-resident active duty service members with out-of-state registration (new legal_basis quote) and the Moving Personal Property page's note that a Virginia State Inspection follows registration.

s2: the deadline field implied the May 1 return date applies to new residents. § 58.1-3518 sets May 1 for property owned on January 1; for a vehicle that gains a situs mid-year, § 58.1-3516(B) says the proration ordinance 'shall provide for the filing of returns' (new legal_basis quote). The field now says this and that the ordinance was not read. Added the Moving page's statement that you must contact the county about a move in or out.

s9: the draft could be read as letting January photos replace the repair estimate. Form f4 always requires the itemized estimate on letterhead (with the preparer's name, address, phone and signature and each condition's effect on value); photos taken in January are an alternative only to the estimate stating that the damage existed in January. Added that the Department reviews and notifies you, and that any refund comes when the appeal process is complete.

s10: the draft listed the contents of a correction request as if required. The county gives no required contents for a correction request; the list comes from the appeal-rights sheet's requirements for administrative appeals. The step now says so, completes the list (federal tax ID, power of attorney or letter of representation) and gives the sheet's mailing address.

s4: added from the exemptions page and form f3 that a vehicle owned by a married couple qualifies if either spouse is the veteran, that f3 accepts VA documentation of payment at 100% as unemployable and documentation already held by the Real Estate Division, and that you reapply only when the vehicle changes; added from Va. Code § 58.1-3668(C) (new legal_basis quote) that the exemption ends at the veteran's death. Added the county's existing volunteer fire and EMS program, quoted from the Legistar 26-381 staff report (new local legal_basis quote).

s8: added from the Supplemental Bills page that a supplemental bill may include three prior years and the current year, and the automatic extension that § 58.1-3916 says the locality 'shall allow' for service members deployed outside the United States.
Fees: added the Debt Set-Off fee ($25 county fee; the Department of Taxation also takes 4%), quoted from the Important Dates and Deadlines page.

Escalation: the Tax Commissioner rung for trailers, campers, RVs, boats and airplanes now notes that the Tax Commissioner may not decide valuation questions for such property (Va. Code § 58.1-3983.1(D)(5), new legal_basis quote). The any-time appeal of an unpaid bill now carries § 58.1-3980(B)'s condition of 'clear factual evidence'. The collection-hold rung now says the hold is automatic under § 58.1-3916 rather than something you ask for. The unsourced '(16th Judicial Circuit)' was dropped from the Circuit Court rung.

Caveat on Legistar 26-381 corrected: the item was introduced August 24, 2026 and, per its Legistar history, 'was scheduled with the Consent Agenda' on September 16, 2026 (not 'in August'); the staff report also says the county already runs an uncodified program. Caveat on unread forms now names the paper aircraft registration form. Sources now list the 26-381 staff report text and the 21-461 matter record.
open_issues: www.albemarle.org blocks automated requests (HTTP 403), so every county page and PDF was checked against Internet Archive snapshots from March to September 2026, not the live site. Changes since then (for example a new relief percentage or fee) would not show.

The County Code text was not read (Municode's terms forbid automated access): any deadline or penalty in § 15-801 for registering a vehicle after moving in or buying, the license-fee rules for new vehicles and proration (§§ 15-1402, 15-1405) and the supplemental-bill due date (21-461 proposed 45 days; adoption not confirmed) remain unknown. The steps say these are unknown rather than asserting them.
The 2026 car tax relief percentage was not found (the exemptions page lists rates through 2025).
The online registration form (f2) and both aircraft forms were not read.
The outcome of the Legistar 26-381 hearings on a $0.00 rate and license fee for volunteer fire and EMS members, and the terms of the county's current volunteer program, were not found.
